title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Reference Architectures, Packaging, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade & Rollback
author: Ava Martinez
summary: Canonical reference for Redwood private deployments covering VPC and on-prem reference architectures, packaging and installer options (including air-gapped installs), day-2 operational procedures, upgrade and rollback playbooks, and a curated customer requirements library.
body:
Overview

This document consolidates guidance for private (VPC and on-prem) deployments of Redwood Inference. It is intended for platform engineers, SREs, customer success engineers, and partners executing or supporting production deployments. It complements the Private Deployments Playbook and the Customer Requirements Library.

Scope and audience

- Scope: Reference architectures, network/security requirements, packaging formats, day-2 operations checklist, controlled upgrade + rollback procedures, and a customer requirements matrix with recommended configurations.
- Audience: Platform/SRE engineers, Solutions and Onboarding teams, Customer infra engineers.

Key services and components

- redwood-control-plane — management/control components (deploys, rollouts, auth).
- redwood-runtime — inference serving runtime (GPU/CPU workers, batching).
- redwood-proxy — ingress layer (TLS termination, per-route routing).
- redwood-metrics — metrics + tracing collector (Prometheus/OTel).
- redwood-kms-connector — KMS/HSM integration shim.
- redwood-store — optional object store connector for model artifacts (S3/GCS/MinIO).

Prerequisites / assumptions

- Customer provides: VPC/subnets or on-prem network zoning, DNS, certificate authority (or ability to provision certs), KMS or HSM if required by policy, and node hardware (if on-prem).
- Access: Admin SSH and Kubernetes cluster admin (if using k8s installer) during install window.
- Compliance: Confirm data residency and audit log requirements before installation (see Customer Requirements Library section).

Network & security requirements (high-level)

| Requirement | Details / Recommendation | Owner | Notes |
|-------------|--------------------------|-------|-------|
| Control plane access | TLS (mTLS recommended), restrict to management CIDRs | Customer / Redwood | Use client cert rotation; require IP allowlist for initial bootstrap |
| Node egress | Allow outbound to Redwood update and telemetry endpoints (whitelisted FQDNs) | Customer | For air-gapped installs, provide artifact bundle |
| Ports | 443/TCP (ingress API), 8443/TCP (internal control plane), 9090/TCP (metrics) | Customer | Map to LB or internal ELB per architecture |
| KMS integration | TLS to KMS endpoint, optional HSM network zone | Customer / Security | Support for AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, and On-Prem HSM via redwood-kms-connector |

Reference architecture — VPC (managed cloud)

Architecture summary:
- Minimal deployment: 3 control-plane nodes (HA), 2+ runtime pools (small and gpu), external NLB/ALB for redwood-proxy, private subnets for runtime workers, public subnets for admin endpoints if required.
- Typical AWS layout: Public subnets (NAT/Jump hosts), Private subnets (control plane & runtime), DB subnet (if using managed DB for metadata), S3 endpoints for model artifacts, KMS in same region.

Operational notes:
- Autoscaling: Runtime pools should be backed by ASG/nodepool scaling tuned to workload (target CPU/GPU utilization 60-75%).
- Multi-AZ: Distribute control plane across 3 AZs for 99.9% availability target.
- Cross-region DR: Use active/passive control plane or configuration replication for critical customers.

Reference architecture — On-Prem (rack / private cloud)

Architecture summary:
- Control plane in a management VLAN, runtime workers in GPU VLANs, load balancer in edge VLAN.
- Storage: Local NFS/MinIO or customer object store; prefer iSCSI/fast NVMe for model cache.

Hardware guidance (on-prem):
- Control plane: 3x VMs (4vCPU, 16GB RAM, 100GB disk) or small bare-metal equivalents.
- Small inference nodes (CPU): 8vCPU, 64GB RAM, 500GB SSD.
- GPU nodes: NVIDIA A10/A100 family recommended; 256GB RAM per GPU host recommended for large models.

Packaging & install options

1) Helm (Kubernetes) — recommended for cloud and private k8s clusters
   - Values example:

replicaCount.controlPlane: 3
runtime.pool.gpu.replicas: 2
ingress.type: LoadBalancer
persistence.backend: s3

2) Installer (kustomize + manifests) — for environments without helm policy

3) Air-gapped bundle — tarball with images, manifests, and offline artifacts. Requires pre-shared image registry or local container registry.

Packaging notes:
- All packages signed; verify GPG signatures on offline bundles.
- Provide image digests for pinned deploys to ensure reproducible installs.

Day-2 operations (daily/weekly checklist)

Daily:
- Check control plane health: kubectl get pods --namespace redwood; expected 100% Ready.
- Verify metrics: P95 latency, token throughput, and error rates in dashboards.
- Backups: Confirm model metadata and postgres snapshots completed successfully.

Weekly:
- Rotate client certs (if using short-lived certs) or validate rotation automation.
- Review audit logs for anomalies.
- Capacity review: check node utilization and autoscaling events.

Runbook excerpts (examples)

- Scaling up GPU pool:
  1. Create new nodepool with label runtime=gpu.
  2. Update runtime pool desired replicas: kubectl apply -f runtime-pool-gpu.yaml.
  3. Monitor new pods: kubectl -n redwood rollout status deploy/redwood-runtime-gpu.

- Adding a new model to object store:
  1. Upload artifact to S3/MinIO and update model registry: POST /v1/models {name, uri, checksum}.
  2. Validate rollout via /v1/models/<name>/status.

Upgrade procedure (controlled rollout)

Principles:
- Stage upgrades: control plane first (canary), then non-critical runtime pools, then GPU pools.
- Keep pinned artifacts and the ability to rollback to prior image digest.
- Minimize in-flight requests to avoid KV cache inconsistencies.

Preflight (automated checks):
- Confirm backups: metadata DB snapshot, model store snapshot, and TLS cert backups exist.
- Confirm health: all pods Ready, no ongoing rollouts, error rate < 0.5% last 15m.
- Confirm disk space > 20% free on control plane nodes.

Step-by-step (example Helm-based upgrade):
1. Create canary control plane release: bump image tag for redwood-control-plane, set replicaCount.canary=1.
2. Monitor control plane canary for 30m; run smoke tests (login, deploy model, one inference).
3. If canary healthy, incrementally roll rest of control plane (3 -> 3 updated).
4. Proceed to runtime pools: upgrade a single non-critical pool (e.g., small-cpu) and validate performance for 60m.
5. Upgrade GPU pools in waves: 1/3 nodes at a time. Confirm model warmup and cache priming before moving to next wave.
6. Post-upgrade: run end-to-end regression prompts and compare quality metrics to baseline.

Rollback procedure (if upgrade fails)

When to rollback:
- Canary fails smoke tests, control plane errors > 1% sustained, or critical latency regressions detected.

Immediate rollback steps (Helm example):
1. Abort ongoing rollout: helm rollback redwood-control-plane <previous-release>.
2. Revert runtime pools by applying pinned image digests.
3. If stateful migration was applied, restore DB snapshot following the DB restore runbook.
4. Notify stakeholders (ops, customer contact) with incident channel and include logs and timeline.

Post-rollback validation:
- Verify control plane and runtime pods are Ready.
- Re-run smoke tests and confirm baseline performance.

Customer requirements library (summary matrix)

| Requirement category | Common ask | Recommended Redwood config / note | Priority |
|---------------------|------------|------------------------------------|----------|
| Data residency | Keep inference & logs in EU only | Deploy in EU region, set object store endpoints in EU, enable restricted retention | High |
| Audit & compliance | Detailed audit logs and WORM storage | Enable audit logging in control plane, ship to customer SIEM or S3 with immutability policy | High |
| Network isolation | No public egress from runtime nodes | Use private subnets, NAT for controlled egress or air-gapped bundle | Medium |
| KMS/HSM | Keys managed by customer HSM | Enable redwood-kms-connector and configure TLS, provide CA certs | High |
| Offline install | Air-gapped installation | Provide tarball with image digests and offline registry, document install steps | Medium |

Known limitations & notes

- On-prem GPU availability: performance depends heavily on GPU family and PCIe topology. Expect tuning per customer.
- Cache warmup after restart: large models can require several minutes of traffic to reach steady token cost; use synthetic priming scripts when possible.

Monitoring & SLOs (recommended)

- Availability (control plane): 99.9% monthly.
- Inference latency: p95 < 250ms for 512-token requests on tuned GPU pools (customer dependent).
- Error rate: < 1% per API method (adjust for customer SLA).

Configuration snippets (examples)

Helm values (example):
controlPlane:
  image: ghcr.io/redwood-inference/control-plane@sha256:abcdef
  replicaCount: 3
runtime:
  pools:
    small:
      replicas: 4
    gpu:
      replicas: 2

Kustomize overlay example: set nodeSelector and tolerations for GPU pools.
